a: QUIC is a UDP-based transport with built-in TLS and faster connection setup.
HTTP/3 reduces head-of-line blocking and improves performance on lossy networks.
TLS 1.3 is faster and safer than older TLS versions with fewer round trips.
ALPN negotiates application protocol (h2/h3) during TLS handshake.
0-RTT can send data on reconnect but has replay considerations.
HTTP/2 multiplexes many streams on one TCP connection.
HTTP/2 server push is rarely used and often disabled; prefer preload hints.
WebSockets traditionally need HTTP/1.1 upgrade; alternatives exist with HTTP/2/3 designs.
DoH encrypts DNS queries over HTTPS for privacy.
Encrypted Client Hello aims to hide more handshake metadata from observers.
